atoms.b: ((Contrary)) to the American Dream, the USA is actually considered one of the least ((socially_mobile)) societies. This is partly because good ((education)) comes at a very high cost and especially ((minorities)) are not provided with equal opportunities.

instruction.text: Choose which term best fits this case study.

atoms.text: Max arrived in the USA with little money and took a job on a factory floor. At night, he studied accounting and saved every spare dollar. He opened a small construction business that steadily grew. Years later, he owned a home, employed others, and called it success.

atoms.a: Which aspects of the American Dream are described?

atoms.text: Minh came to the USA in order to provide a better life for herself and her daughter than she had previously been able to lead in Vietnam. Upon arrival, she faced countless obstacles that made it impossible for her to access upward social mobility. As an Asian woman not fluent in English, she was confronted with prejudice and very few job opportunities.

atoms.a: Which aspects of the American Nightmare are described?

atoms.text: Holly's mother works as a cleaner and her father works as a bus driver. Because these are lower income jobs, the family does not have enough money to support Holly and her sister's education and they struggle to make ends meet every month. There is no improvement in sight, as the parents do not qualify for higher paying jobs.
